paras: The masked men's seizure of the Davis murder pistol was an episode in Tennessee in May 1882 in which eight masked men went at night to the cabin of a Black woman and, with threats, demanded a pistol she had found near the scene of a recent murder. Told that her landlord, Mr. Phelps, had it, they called him to his window and took it from him; no one was reported hurt. The McMinnville New Era, whose item was reprinted in Winchester, treated the episode as a likely sign that the band knew something about the killing of Capt. James M. Davis.

Capt. James M. Davis had recently been "assassinated" in the neighborhood, and the killing was unsolved when the item appeared. On a Wednesday evening a "negro woman" who lived nearby on Phelps's place was gathering ginseng in the woods close to the murder site when she found a large navy pistol with every chamber loaded. She took it home and gave it to Phelps.

Two days later, on Friday night, eight masked men came to her cabin and demanded the pistol. When she said she did not have it, they demanded "with threats" to know where it was, and she told them Phelps had it. The men then went to Phelps's house, called him to the window and demanded the pistol, which he handed to them through the window.

No report of an arrest or of any inquiry into the masked men appears in the coverage, and no further report of the Davis case was found. The New Era wrote that it "might have been fortunate for the ends of justice" had Phelps given the pistol to the authorities, though it allowed that most people in his place would have done as he did.

The only known account is the McMinnville New Era's item, reprinted on 17 May 1882 in the Winchester Home Journal under the headline "The Davis Murderers." The editor reasoned that the men demanding the pistol "were engaged in or were in possession of facts concerning the killing of Davis" and feared it might help find them out, and closed with the hope that the pistol "may yet furnish a clue" to the murderers. The item identified the woman only by race, never by name, and said nothing further about the threats made against her.

accounts.label: McMinnville New Era (reprinted)
accounts.gist: Eight masked men threatened the woman to learn where the pistol was and took it from Phelps; the editor supposed they were tied to the Davis killing and hoped the pistol might still furnish a clue.

framing.detail: Under the headline 'The Davis Murderers' the item framed the episode as part of an unsolved murder case, regretting that Phelps had not given the pistol to the authorities; it says nothing about the threat to the woman beyond reporting it.

record_check.dossier: 'Last Friday night' in a New Era item of unknown date, reprinted 1882-05-17; 1882-05-12 is plausible but not stated
No county is named; Warren is an inference from the McMinnville New Era source
An unnamed Black woman (threatened) and Mr. Phelps (made to surrender the pistol)
The woman is called a 'negro woman'; Phelps's race is not stated
None stated by the men; the paper supposed they wanted to recover evidence in the Davis killing

info: A Friday night, two days after the pistol was found on a Wednesday; the item calls it 'Last Friday night' relative to the New Era's (unseen) issue date, so the night fell shortly before 1882-05-17, likely 1882-05-12 or a week earlier
A Black woman's cabin on Mr. Phelps's place, near where Capt. James M. Davis had been assassinated, and Phelps's house; no town or county is named, though the report came from the McMinnville New Era
An unnamed 'negro woman' living on Phelps's place, threatened; Mr. Phelps, made to hand over the pistol
Masked men, unidentified; the paper supposed they were 'engaged in or were in possession of facts concerning the killing of Davis'

sources.note: Reprint of a McMinnville New Era item, 'The Davis Murderers': eight masked men threatened a Black woman at her cabin to recover a pistol she found near the Davis murder site, then got it from Phelps.
quotes: Last Friday night, two days after the pistol was found, eight masked men went to her cabin and demanded the pistol; she told them that she did not have it.
